description: Violet stone cut with a knot that has no end. Scholars want it, argue over it, and cannot say what it fell out of.
lore: People bring this one to [[characters/cfe826c1|Jehanne]] to be read. Not valued — the scholars do the valuing, and they have bid it past two hundred and fifty on the strength of what it does, which is simple enough: whatever you can do, you can do again sooner, and it lands harder than it did the first time. What they want read is the figure. Deep violet, cut clean through with an interlace that crosses itself four times and closes, no end anywhere in it and no place where it begins.

She tells them the same thing every time and it costs her a little more each time: it belongs to no rite she keeps, it is in none of her books, and she cannot say what it means. They keep coming. Belief is thin in this country and the appetite underneath it is not, and a closed figure looks so much like something meant that a man will carry it a day's walk to be told what. She knows precisely what she is being used as. She does it anyway, which is the whole of her.

Asked a fourth time in one evening she once said more than she intended. A figure like that, she said, is what you get when a thing has gone the same round long enough that it has stopped needing anyone at the far end of it — then she got up to see to the fire, and she has not repeated it since. It is still the only reading anyone has offered, and no grader will put it on a card. [[lore/the_hard_pieces|The rule everybody learns first]] says something was going round. Nobody in the trade can produce it.
gm_notes: Unbound stone, handled through appetite for meaning rather than provenance or price — the shipped line said 'nobody can say what died to leave it', which breaks two house words, so the look was kept and the claim rephrased. Deliberately does not re-run the frost rune's argument that a soulstone cannot be worked; nobody here asks how the knot got there, only what it says. Jehanne's reading is a description of stage Habit and also, unmistakably, of her own practice, and she leaves the room rather than hear it back. Nothing is asserted to exist and no creature is invented.
